To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of dynamic logic and DLP provides a powerful and clear formalism to specify and realize complex behavior patterns for embodied agents, and that the combination of DLP and a rich media environment provides the computational support for realizing the complex behavioral patterns.

1) a scripting language for embodied agents should have clear semantics; 2) DLP is a good platform for implementing such a language; 3) the implementation of a language for embodied agents is a challenging task, in particular with respect to the parallel actions and synchronization; and 4) our approach can be used to create reusable libraries of behavioral patters.
we developed a scripting language for embodied agents that is based on dynamic (temporal) logic and is implemented in a VRML/X3DMiddleware based on distributed logic programming.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework that supports the specification and implementation of embodied agents in VRML/X 3D-based environments in a declarative way.
the implementation and use of embodied agents in a rich media environment.

the design of a scripting language that allows for the creation and composition of complex behavioral patterns for embodied agents in a VRML/X3d environment, as well as the development of an implementation that provides the necessary computational support for this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach allows for an effective and efficient development of embodied agents in 3D environments.
the implementation of the proposed approach is feasible and that the results of the research project are very encouraging.
we have developed a framework that allows for the creation and reuse of behavioral patterns for embodied agents in VRML/XD-based environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how a clear and formal specification of behavioral patterns may be realized in a distributed logic programming framework.
we have shown the feasibility of our approach, which is based on a combination of a clear semantics of the behavioral patterns and an efficient implementation in a rich 3D environment.
we have developed a platform for the creation and execution of complex behaviors for embodied agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DLP in combination with dynamic logic allows for a declarative and modular approach for creating embodied agents.

DLP can provide a solid computational platform for the implementation of complex behavior patterns, which can be used to develop reusable libraries of behavior patterns for a range of applications, such as instructional virtual reality.

the use of a formal specification language, in combination with a platform that supports the computational aspects, is a viable way of developing complex embodied agents in VRML/XD3-based 3D environments.
